label: models/fw_drum.mdl: a rusted 55-gallon drum with a hazard stripe

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_longjump.mdl, models/rip.mdl, models/uplant1.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, C, B, D where the asset was D, A, C, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: All ten views show one upright cylinder with a slightly domed lid and a flat base, with no part sticking out or missing. The top and below views are round, as the brief's drum should be. The outline matches the brief's words.

M2.reason: Measured size 23.2 x 23.2 x 35.5 against the brief's 23 across and 34 high: 0.9% off across and 4.4% off in height, within 15%.

M3.reason: Parts the brief implies for a 55-gallon drum: the lid with two bungs (both visible as pale hex plugs in the top and front-left views), two rolling hoops above and below the stripe, and the top and bottom rims. All are present in the right places. The drum has no handles, tabs or claws to miss.

M4.reason: Rust-brown painted steel over the body and lid, the bungs in pale steel, and a yellow and black hazard band as the brief asks. Each region reads as the same material and colour family across the views.

M5.reason: Rust mottling, the hazard stripe and the hoop bands are all there and sharp enough. In the front and front-left views a vertical seam runs through the stripe at about the middle of the front, where the stripe's pattern changes across it. That is a visible texture-seam fault on the stripe, not a shape fault.

M6.reason: In the four line-up readings the asset was never picked as the one not made by Valve (judges picked C, C, B, D where the asset was D, A, C, C), so it passes for one of the game's. M6 is capped at 2 by the rubric.

M7.reason: Upright, standing on its origin at the base, and the hazard band is on the front-facing side as a drum's front would be. Nothing is turned or floating.

M8.reason: The GoldSrc check reported no errors. 336 triangles is under the most Half-Life spends on a prop of its kind and size (422), and under twice the median (198) it passes against the amended rule's bar. Views from above and below show the lid and base closed, with the bungs seated on the lid and nothing open or floating.
